newsitem.title: UK: Euro, Singapore, US refining margins slump in Aug.
newsitem.headline: Euro, Singapore, US refining margins slump in Aug.

text.p: Refining margins around the world fell sharply in August as product prices failed to keep pace with rising crude markets, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
Sour crude margins in the Mediterranean were hit hardest, falling by more than $2 a barrel from July highs before making a strong recovery toward the end of the month.
Mediterranean Urals topping margins fell 80 cents on the month to average a loss of two cents a barrel. Urals cracking margins fell 68 cents to a profit of $1.31, the IEA said.
Brent margins in Rotterdam also fell heavily, down 68 cents for topping to a four-cent loss and down 54 cents to a $1.23 profit for cracking.
U.S. Gulf Coast margins saw a sharp 79-cent decline for cracking Brent to a 59-cent profit and a 44-cent fall in WTI cracking to a 50-cent profit.
Singapore margin declines were less severe but topping margins stayed negative.
Dubai hydroskimming fell four cents for a 43-cent loss and Dubai cracking fall 42 cents to a $1.32 profit.
